VALUATION_METHODS._AdditionalDescription:
TREMONTON CITY: Tremonton lies in the Bear River Valley in northeastern part of Box Elder County. The Malad River flows through the city. Tremonton is located near the junction of Interstate 15 and Interstate 84. It is bordered on the north by the city of Garland, with which it is closely associated. Tremonton is the second largest community in Box Elder County and is about 12 miles northwest of Brigham City and has a estimated population of 7,790. It was settled in 1888 but was largely uninhabited until the early 1900’s. It was incorporated in 1906 with a population of about 350. The majority of the early growth came between 1950 and 1970 and then again from 1990 to 2010. There is a correlation between the grow cycles and the predominate age of homes in the area. There is a small business district and somewhat limited commercial services. Tremonton has two elementary schools, McKinley Elementary and North Park. Older students attend Alice C. Harris Intermediate in Tremonton, as well as Bear River Middle School and Bear River High School. Thiokol Corporation (ATK) has a current Utah base employment of approximately 4,500+ located about 18 miles west of Tremonton. ATK is a large defense contractor. Autoliv has a large plant in Brigham City. Autoliv is a manufacturer of airbags for the automobile industry. Recently several businesses have moved to the area including Proctor & Gamble's paper plant, Wal-Mart distribution center. Also, a major breakfast cereal manufacturing and distribution plant recently began operations in Tremonton. Nucor Steal and Vulcraft have the same parent company and are in steel production and truss fabrication.
GENERAL MARKET & ECONOMIC CONDITION IN UTAH: As reported by the Utah State Governor's office and Utah Department of Workforce Services updated April 2022. Employment Change: Utah’s nonagricultural employment was the 1st most favorable in December 2021 with an increase of 4.2% compared to the nationally, employment decreased of -1.8%. Unemployment: Utah’s December 2021 unemployment rate is the 1st lowest in the nation at 2.1% and better than the national unemployment rate of 3.8%. Workforce: Utah has the 6th highest labor force participation rate in the US. Household Income: Utah’s household income is 5th highest in the nation at $83,670 compared to the US $67,521. Poverty Rate: poverty level is the 2nd lowest in the nation at 7.1%. Demographic: Utah has the youngest median age at 31.3 years old compared to the national median age of 38.2 years old. Utah also has the largest household size at 3.08 compared to the national household size of 2.61. Home Prices: According to the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) House Price Appreciation Ranking, Utah’s house prices were up 26.5% in the Third quarter of 2022 from the Third quarter of 2020. Median home sale price in Utah is $497,100 and the Ogden-Clearfield MSA has a median home sale price of $434,400 (+24%). Logan, MSA has a median home sale price of 417,9000 (+30.6%) Building Permits: The top five counties building permit in 2021 were Salt Lake (8,862), Utah (10,894), Washington (3,297, Davis (3,367) and Weber (1,658). Interest Rates: The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage averaged 3.6% for the week ending Jan 31, 2022 Foreclosure Rates: As reported by RealtyTrac Utah has an average foreclosure rate of 0.008%, The Utah foreclosure rate is higher than the national average of 0.0149%. Coincident Index: Utah’s December 2021 Coincident index was 160.2 which is the largest (best) in the nation. The national coincident index for November 2021 was 131.8. The coincident indexes combine four state-level indicators to summarize current economic conditions in a single statistic. The four state-level variables in each coincident index are nonfarm payroll employment, average hours worked in manufacturing by production workers, the unemployment rate, and wage and salary disbursements plus proprietors' income deflated by the consumer price index (U.S. city average). The trend for each state’s index is set to the trend of its gross domestic product (GDP), so long-term growth in the state’s index matches long-term growth in its GDP.

SALES_COMPARISON._Comment: The comparable sales selected are the most similar disclosed sales. Adjustments reflect the different features as valued by the market and not the cost of the amenity. Typically these differences included: size, parking, baths, fireplaces, jetted tubs, out buildings, etc. Differences in GLA were adjusted $60p/sf, which was derived as follows: Replacement cost new (Marshal&Swift/Local builder) less physical depreciation (ref to cost apprch) less market difference of 60% ($184.38-20%=$147.50-60%=$59.00 ($60r) basement shell at $30p/sf and finish by room count for utility rather than percent of finish. The number of rooms contribute more to value than does the percentage of finish and real estate agents tend to more accurately report the number of finished rooms than correctly estimating the percent of finish. Adjusted value range from sales comparison approach is $353,000 to $359,000(r) See additional comps and comments on next page. See comments on page 3. An attempt was made to bracket all areas of value as the market determines, i.e garage, fireplace, cooling, age, lot size & utility etc. Comparable provided as a bracketing comparable. Comp #5 is a current active listing provided as part of clients scope of work. No consideration was given this listing as it is not a closed sale. In the opinion of this appraiser the comparable sales presented best represent the subjects value.
